input.plan:
# Faster media scans

Rescans re-walk the library and, for every TV episode, run `ffmpeg.probe` only to read a title tag ([app/database/media_metadata_collector.py](app/database/media_metadata_collector.py) `build_tv_show` → `get_ffmpeg_metadata`). Each insert then commits on its own ([app/database/db_access.py](app/database/db_access.py) `execute_db_query`). `INSERT OR IGNORE` already keeps the first title, `added_at`, and cover, so a later scan cannot update those fields anyway.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  walk[rglob mp4] --> known{content_src already in catalog}
  known -->|yes| skip[Skip file]
  known -->|no| kind{TV movie or book}
  kind -->|TV| probe[ffprobe title tag]
  kind -->|movie or book| name[Filename only]
  probe --> write[One transaction for that file]
  name --> write
```

## Skip catalogued files before probe

In [app/database/db_getter.py](app/database/db_getter.py) `collect_directory_content`, load `content_src` once via the existing `get_all_content_paths()` into a set.

Pass that set into `collect_mp4_files`. After the relative `content_src` is computed and before `build_tv_show` / `build_movie` / `build_book`, skip paths already in the set. New TV files still get `ffprobe`. Movies and books are unchanged except they also skip the stat/insert work on rescan.

Yield from `rglob` directly instead of `list(p.rglob(...))`.

## One commit per new file

Add a small batch flag on `DBConnection`: while it is set, `execute_db_query` executes but does not commit. `scan_content_directories` / `collect_directory_content` wraps each new file's `insert_container_content` in one batch and commits when that file finishes (rollback that file on error, then continue). Other callers keep today's per-statement commit. One transaction for the whole library would hold the SQLite write lock across a first scan and block playback progress updates.

## Reuse container and tag ids inside one scan

A first scan of a show still inserts the same season/show row and the same few tags once per episode. Keep a dict on the handler for the duration of `scan_content_directories`:

- `(container_title, container_path)` → id
- `tag_title` → id

`insert_container` and `insert_tag` consult it before `INSERT` + follow-up `SELECT`. Clear it when the scan ends. This is scan-local; browse and playback queries stay as they are.

## Tests

Add a unit test (memory DB, mocked `get_ffmpeg_metadata`) that:

- the first scan of a TV file calls probe once and stores the probed title
- the second scan of the same `content_src` does not call probe and leaves the stored title and `added_at` unchanged
- a new episode of the same show is still inserted and probed

Run `pytest tests/ -m "not integration" -q`.

No schema bump and no README change: catalog contents stay the same; only unchanged files are no longer rewritten.

todos.content: Skip already-catalogued content_src before ffprobe and yield rglob
Commit once per new file during scan only
Cache container and tag ids for the duration of a scan
Unit-test first scan vs rescan probe behavior

questions.prompt: Q1 — Already-catalogued files. A rescan cannot update title, cover, or added_at anyway (INSERT OR IGNORE). Skipping the whole file also skips ffprobe and the insert chain. It will not repair a file whose content row exists but whose show/season link never got written. What should a rescan do with a content_src that is already in the catalog?

options.label: Skip the whole file (recommended)
Skip ffprobe only; still INSERT OR IGNORE
Keep probing and inserting every file

questions.prompt: Q2 — New TV files. Probe exists only to copy the MP4 title tag. If the tag is missing, the title becomes "Episode N" from the filename. Movies and books never probe. What should the first insert of a TV file do?

options.label: ffprobe once, on first insert only (recommended)
Never probe; title is always Episode N from the filename

questions.prompt: Q3 — Commit size. Today every statement commits and fsyncs. One transaction for the whole library would block playback-progress writes until the scan finishes. What commit scope do you want for new files?

options.label: One transaction per new file (recommended)
One transaction for the whole scan
Leave per-statement commits

questions.prompt: Q4 — First-scan write amplification. The same show, season, and tag rows are inserted once per episode. An in-memory id cache for that scan cuts those repeats. It does nothing for a rescan if known files are skipped. Include it in this change?

options.label: Yes, cache container and tag ids for the scan (recommended)
No, skip the cache; known-file skip is enough

questions.prompt: Q5 — Files that disappeared. The catalog never deletes a row when the MP4 is gone. This change does not have to take that on. Should a scan remove catalog rows whose files are no longer on disk?

options.label: Leave orphans; do not delete rows (recommended)
Remove catalog rows whose files are gone

content.text: Those answers change the commit groups and add deletion. I’ll check how rows are tied together so the next questions are about real constraints.

questions.prompt: Q6 — TV transaction size. You want fewer commits than one per episode: all movies in one transaction, all books in one transaction, and TV grouped as shows. For TV, which group is one commit? A show with hundreds of episodes holds the SQLite write lock until that group finishes, so playback-progress updates wait.

options.label: One transaction per show (all of its episodes) (recommended)
One transaction for every TV file in the folder

questions.prompt: Q7 — A grouped commit fails. Example: episode 40 of a show raises while that show's transaction is open, or one movie fails inside the movies transaction. What should the scan do?

options.label: Roll back that group only, then continue with the next show or the next kind (recommended)
Roll back that group and stop the scan

questions.prompt: Q8 — Missing disk. Foreign keys are declared but never turned on, so a delete does not cascade by itself. content_src is unique per catalog row and each row has a content_directory_id. If a media root is unmounted, rglob sees nothing. Treating that as "all files gone" would delete that directory's catalog. When should a scan delete rows?

options.label: Only for a content directory whose root exists and whose walk finished; a missing root skips pruning for that directory (recommended)
Delete anything not seen, even if the root is missing

questions.prompt: Q9 — Empty shows and seasons. Deleting a content row leaves container_content, user_tags_content, and the season/show containers behind (no ON DELETE CASCADE, and foreign_keys is off). Play count and resume position live on the content row and go away with it. A file that returns later is inserted as new. After removing missing files, what else should go?

options.label: Also delete link rows and season/show containers that have no episodes left. Keep the tag vocabulary (recommended)
Delete the content row only; leave containers and link rows

questions.prompt: Q10 — One file fails. Commits are one transaction per file again. Pruning a directory is a separate transaction after that directory's walk finishes. If a file's inserts fail, or a directory's prune fails, what should happen?

options.label: Roll back that file or that directory's deletes, then continue the rest of the scan (recommended)
Roll back that unit and stop the scan

questions.prompt: Q11 — Which rows count as missing. The scanner only walks tv_shows/, movies/, and books/ under each content root. A catalog row outside those prefixes is never yielded, so a naive "not seen" delete would remove it. Foreign keys are off, so the prune must explicitly delete container_content and user_tags_content for the dropped content, then delete season/show containers that have no children left. Play count and resume position on a deleted row are gone. Which rows may be deleted?

options.label: Only rows under tv_shows/, movies/, or books/ for a root that exists and finished walking, when that path was not yielded (recommended)
Any catalog row whose content_src was not yielded, including paths outside those three folders

"""Scan skips ffprobe for catalogued TV files and commits one file at a time."""
import os
import pathlib
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest import mock

from app.database.db_access import DBType
from app.database.db_getter import DBHandler


def _probe(path, content_data):
    content_data["content_title"] = "Probed Title"


class TestMediaScan(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self._tmpdir = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
        self.root = pathlib.Path(self._tmpdir.name) / "library"
        self.show_dir = self.root / "tv_shows" / "Demo Show"
        self.show_dir.mkdir(parents=True)
        self._write_episode(1)
        self.db_path = os.path.join(self._tmpdir.name, "scan.db")
        self.db = DBHandler(db_type=DBType.PHYSICAL, file_name=self.db_path)
        self.db.open()
        self.db.create_db()
        self.db.add_content_directory_info(
            {
                "content_src": self.root.as_posix(),
                "content_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/",
            }
        )

    def tearDown(self):
        self.db.close()
        self._tmpdir.cleanup()

    def _write_episode(self, number):
        path = self.show_dir / f"Demo Show - s01e0{number}.mp4"
        path.write_bytes(b"")
        return path

    def _content_row(self, src_suffix):
        return self.db.get_data_from_db_first_result(
            "SELECT content_title, added_at FROM content WHERE content_src = :content_src;",
            {"content_src": src_suffix},
        )

    def test_rescan_skips_probe_and_keeps_title(self):
        with mock.patch(
            "app.database.media_metadata_collector.get_ffmpeg_metadata",
            side_effect=_probe,
        ) as probe:
            self.db.scan_content_directories()
            self.assertEqual(probe.call_count, 1)
            first = self._content_row("/tv_shows/Demo Show/Demo Show - s01e01.mp4")
            self.assertEqual(first["content_title"], "Probed Title")
            self.assertTrue(first["added_at"])

            self.db.scan_content_directories()
            self.assertEqual(probe.call_count, 1)
            second = self._content_row("/tv_shows/Demo Show/Demo Show - s01e01.mp4")
            self.assertEqual(second["content_title"], "Probed Title")
            self.assertEqual(second["added_at"], first["added_at"])

            self._write_episode(2)
            self.db.scan_content_directories()
            self.assertEqual(probe.call_count, 2)
            new_episode = self._content_row("/tv_shows/Demo Show/Demo Show - s01e02.mp4")
            self.assertEqual(new_episode["content_title"], "Probed Title")

    def test_failed_file_rolls_back_and_scan_continues(self):
        self._write_episode(2)
        original = DBHandler.insert_content

        def fail_second(handler, content):
            original(handler, content)
            if str(content.get("content_src", "")).endswith("s01e02.mp4"):
                raise RuntimeError("boom")

        with mock.patch(
            "app.database.media_metadata_collector.get_ffmpeg_metadata",
            side_effect=_probe,
        ):
            with mock.patch.object(DBHandler, "insert_content", fail_second):
                self.db.scan_content_directories()

        kept = self._content_row("/tv_shows/Demo Show/Demo Show - s01e01.mp4")
        dropped = self._content_row("/tv_shows/Demo Show/Demo Show - s01e02.mp4")
        self.assertEqual(kept["content_title"], "Probed Title")
        self.assertEqual(dropped, {})
